summary:
Earth2Moon is an interactive web platform that uses NASA data and artificial intelligence to find places on Earth whose terrain resembles the Moon and Mars. Before rovers, navigation systems or astronauts go to another world, they need realistic places on Earth to train and test. Finding those places today takes a lot of expert knowledge and scattered data.

Our platform takes public NASA datasets on lunar and Martian terrain and compares them with Earth's geographic data. It looks at features such as elevation, slope, craters and rock distribution. A similarity-scoring model then ranks Earth locations against a lunar or Martian landscape the user picks. The results appear on an interactive map, and each site gets a clear explanation of where it matches and where it differs.

Earth can't fully reproduce conditions on other worlds, so Earth2Moon is open about the limits of every match. By turning complex scientific data into a simple, accessible tool, the project helps researchers, students and space enthusiasts get ready for future missions to the Moon and Mars.
details:
What it does and how it works
Earth2Moon, built by team Vision-X, is an AI-assisted geospatial web platform. It ranks sites on Earth by how closely their terrain resembles selected regions of the Moon and Mars. Its tagline is "Find Earth. Explore Beyond."

Users go through five steps:

  1. Select a body: Moon or Mars.
  2. Choose a target region: for example, the area around Shackleton crater at the lunar south pole, or one of three Mars landing sites.
  3. Define a mission: rover mobility testing, navigation or astronaut training. The mission sets how much weight each terrain feature gets.
  4. Configure features: choose and adjust the terrain characteristics to compare.
  5. Run the analysis.

Behind this, a Python data pipeline reads NASA digital elevation models, extracts terrain features, and normalizes them across the three worlds, since their datasets have very different resolutions. A weighted similarity engine then scores candidate Earth sites. K-means clustering groups terrain types, and nearest-neighbor ranking finds the closest matches. Results appear on an interactive map with charts that break down each score. An optional AI summary explains in plain language why each site matches, where it differs, and what it could be used for.

Benefits

  • Makes analog site discovery faster, more transparent and repeatable.
  • Gives explainable results: every score shows which features drove it.
  • Turns NASA's raw scientific data into a tool that students, researchers and space enthusiasts can all use.
  • Ranks sites for a specific mission instead of using one generic score.

Intended impact
We want to help mission planners and researchers find realistic Earth test environments for rovers, navigation systems and astronaut training ahead of future lunar and Martian missions. We also want to open up planetary data to students, especially in Saudi Arabia and the region, so they can explore it themselves.

Tools and technologies

  • Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4, Leaflet (interactive maps), Recharts (score charts), custom SVG
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI, uvicorn, NumPy, scikit-learn (K-means, nearest neighbors)
  • AI summaries: optional integration with Anthropic Claude, OpenAI or Google Gemini
  • NASA data: LRO LOLA gridded DEM (Moon, 40 m), MGS MOLA MEGDR (Mars, ~1.85 km), NASADEM_HGT v001 (Earth, ~30 m), LRO WAC mosaic, Viking MDIM 2.1 and MOLA shaded relief (NASA Solar System Treks), NASA Blue Marble (via NASA GIBS)
  • Basemaps: Esri, OpenStreetMap, CARTO
  • Testing and deployment: pytest, vitest, Docker, Render, GitHub

Creativity
Earth2Moon compares Earth, the Moon and Mars in a single workflow, which turns analog site selection into an "Earth twin" search. Ranking depends on the mission, so the same lunar region can produce different best matches for a rover test than for astronaut training. Instead of a black-box score, it explains each match: feature-by-feature breakdowns plus AI-written summaries. The design is clean and simple, so the scientific data feels approachable.

Factors we considered

  • Scientific honesty: Earth can't reproduce gravity, vacuum, radiation or regolith. We compare only terrain features and state each match's limits clearly. Crater morphology, rock distribution, geological classification and regolith properties are not modeled yet.
  • Data resolution: Elevation data ranges from ~30 m on Earth to ~1.85 km on Mars, so features had to be normalized before comparison.
  • Prototype calibration: Our scoring weights are prototype parameters that still need calibration against known analog sites.
  • Scope: The current version covers the Shackleton region on the Moon, three Mars landing sites, and one Earth tile in Chile's Atacama Desert. The pipeline is built to add more regions.
  • Usability and deployment: A guided five-step flow keeps it usable for non-experts, and Docker and Render make it easy to deploy and reproduce.
